title.narrative: Boosting Productivity Through Human Capital Development Program, Subprogram 2

description.narrative: This program provides a platform for the Asian Development Bank (ADB) support for the government's focus on reducing poverty and inequality through the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to achieve sustainable and inclusive growth. Boosting human capital will be important to address scarring from the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic, including the detrimental effect on education and employment, and to build resilience. The program (i) strengthens policies to finance and monitor the SDGs, (ii) improves educational attainment and skills development, and (iii) enhances social protection and public health systems.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.1. The government continued to implement SDGs by: (i) partnering with universities to establish an additional 11 SDG Centers; (ii) developing the SDGs dashboard to identify subnational governments with performance below the national average for SDG targets, and providing capacity building support; and (iii) issuing the new SDG road map and financing chapter based on the evaluation of the impact of COVID-19 on SDG implementation, including more ambitious targets to improve socioeconomic outcomes for women and youth. (BAPPENAS)
1.2. The government incentivized local governments to meet SDG targets, including stunting, by providing performance-based fiscal transfers. (Ministry of Finance)

1.3. The government: (i) increased capitation payments for primary care services, including maternal health services, provided by puskesmas (from Rp3,600 to Rp9,000 per beneficiary) and by Class D pratama hospital and clinic (from Rp9,000 to Rp16,000 per beneficiary); and (ii) initiated streamlining of non-medical benefits for inpatient care in 14 hospitals, to improve equity of access to quality health care and sustainability of health services. (Ministry of Finance; Ministry of Health)

2.1. The government continued to implement JobStart Indonesia: (i) by providing unemployed youth with demand-based technical training and internship opportunities in Bandung Barat and Makassar; and (ii) by including four additional provinces (Serang, Batang, Serdang and Penjanjam Utara) in the JobStart Indonesia program; (Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs; Ministry of Manpower)

2.2. The government continued implementation of the preemployment card program with its skills development focus through:(i) reaching over 7 million beneficiaries (at least 50% women); and (ii) increasing the training voucher allocation per beneficiary from Rp1 million in 2021 to Rp3.5 million in 2023, to boost efforts to promote productive employment and decent work. (Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, Ministry of Manpower)

2.3. The government issued, through Presidential regulation, its comprehensive TVET Revitalization Strategy, including: (i) creation of an inter-ministerial National Coordination Team to set strategic directions and overall operational guidance for the integrated implementation of the Strategy; (ii) mechanisms to align with requirements and increase roles of business, and industry in TVET service provision; and (iii) requiring the use of SKKNI in developing the TVET learning standards and curriculum. (Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs; Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology; Coordinating Ministry for Human Development and Cultural Affairs)

2.4. The government intensified the use of digital technology to improve teaching and learning by: (i) expanding implementation of the Guru Penggerak program, covering 38,775 teachers (at least 60% women); (ii) introducing Merdeka Mengajar, a digital platform on teaching and learning resources and collaborative learning for teachers and professional learning communities, accessed by 2.9 million teachers (at least 60% women); and (iii) adopting and initiating implementation of a strategy on the use of EdTech in the TVET sector. (Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology)

2.5. The government implemented the digital credentialing system recorded on blockchain and designed by the ICE Institute, in 14 ICE consortium universities and 223 Indonesian universities participating in the ICE Institute online learning platform, to improve male and female learners' access to quality and relevant higher education and enhance school-to-work transition. (Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology)

3.1. The government implemented the unemployment benefit program by: (i) allocating budget to pay the benefits and support program implementation; and (ii) providing beneficiaries of the program with cash benefit, reskilling and upskilling opportunities, and access to career counselling. (Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs; Ministry of Manpower)

3.2. The government strengthened implementation of the conditional cash transfer program, particularly in disadvantaged areas by: (i) streamlining business processes on the delivery of interventions and benefits; and (ii) increasing adaptive beneficiary payment mechanisms, including using the Association of State-Owned Banks for non-cash payments and through PT. POS for cash payments for inclusive finance, covering almost 10 million household beneficiaries, including pregnant and breastfeeding mothers in 2023. (Coordinating Ministry for Human Development, Ministry of Social Affairs)

3.3. The government implemented ILP in puskesmas which includes health kaders monitoring: (i) pregnant mothers to help prevent maternal deaths; and (ii) babies, under-5, and pre-school children, to support the prevention and reduction of stunting. (Ministry of Health)

3.4. The government accelerated implementation of the Health Sector Transformation Agenda, providing budget mapped to the HSTA pillars, to strengthen the health system, particularly its primary care system and its capacity to provide maternal and child health services. (Ministry of Health, Ministry of Finance)
